 Korea Open: American Pursuit Gathers Momentum
 Friday, November 6, 2026
 TEXT BY DIANNE PIERRE | JNANESH SALIAN/BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Lauren Lam / Allison Quynh Lee continued their march towards a historic breakthrough on Friday with a 21-19 21-10 win over Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva at YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 .
 The result marks the Americans’ third Super 500 semifinal of the season, adding to a campaign that has also featured a Super 300 last four appearance. This has established them as genuine contenders on the HSBC BWF World Tour.
 For a pair seeking to become the first American women’s doubles partnership to win a World Tour title, Yeosu represents another significant step forward. It also comes at an important time, with the countdown already underway to the opening of the qualification period for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games next year. With American badminton preparing for a rare moment in the spotlight on home soil, Lam/Lee’s continued rise is providing further evidence that the United States can field genuine challengers when qualification begins.
 The quarterfinal presented a unique challenge. Across the net stood not only accomplished opponents but close friends and long-time idols.
 “It was a fight of the nerves,” Lee said.
 Having spent countless hours together on and off court, both pairs entered the match with a deep understanding of each other’s strengths and tendencies. The opening game reflected that familiarity, with neither side able to establish control. Lam/Lee eventually edged ahead at the crucial moments before taking command in the second game to complete a convincing victory.
 Competing as independent players, the world No.15s’ rise has not happened overnight.
 “We put everything into this,” Lee said. “We put school on hold. We put on hold on a lot of things, like friendships back at home. We still keep in contact but obviously we can’t see them all the time, so a lot of sacrifices.”
 Their success has also coincided with growing momentum for American badminton across several disciplines.
 “I’m really happy we are all kind of raising the bar,” Lam said.
 Despite another career milestone, neither player is looking beyond the next match.
 “We just want to perform well and then everything else will follow,” Lee said.
 That approach has already carried Lam/Lee to another semifinal. Now, with their consistency at Super 500 level becoming impossible to ignore, the prospect of a first World Tour title no longer feels like a distant ambition but an increasingly realistic goal.
 First, they will need to get past Japan’s Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara in the semifinals on Saturday.

 WHAT OTHERS SAID 
 “I do still get nervous. A lot of fans come to see me so I always want to do my best for them. I take each match at a time.” – An Se Young after the 21-7 21-13 win over Riko Gunji extended her winning streak to 53 matches
 “At 19-all (in the first game), I started to choose my attacks more wisely because one-shot winners against him is very, very tough.” – Victor Lai finally got revenge on Yudai Okimoto after two losses, winning 21-19 21-12 to book his place in the semifinals
 “I really didn’t think we would win. It was such a difficult match. We lost the first game but were able to stay focused in the second and third games.” – Kim Yu Jung delighted to defeat Li Yi Jing/Wang Yi Duo 17-21 21-8 22-20 to reach a maiden Super 500 semifinal
 “I watched a lot of his matches against Kento Momota. They were always very exciting. Thrilling, even. I hope to be like one of those players one day.” – Jason Gunawan credits Anthony Sinisuka Ginting for inspiring him after outlasting the Indonesian 23-26 21-11 21-13
 “I will definitely look to learn from him, especially his rhythm when playing his shots, his changes of pace and the threat he creates with his shots. I also want to learn from his approach and the way he thinks about and handles each shot.” – Xie Hao Nan after he and world champion Wang Chang almost got the better of top seeds Kim Won Ho/Seo Seung Jae
 Xie (right) says he and Wang played their best badminton against the Koreans.
